author: jukan05
text:
TrendForce:

System-level testing and validation issues persist on the Rubin platform, with volumes expected to ramp gradually from 4Q26 or 1Q27.

DRAM
Suppliers’ early-stage discussions on 4Q26 contract pricing point to meaningful price increases, suggesting strengthening demand momentum, particularly from US CSPs.

NAND (Enterprise SSDs)
The DRAM shortage is constraining some NAND suppliers’ ability to support enterprise SSD solutions. As a result, enterprise SSDs are expected to remain undersupplied through 2026.

HDD
Even though Toshiba announced a new production line expansion, it will take at least 12 to 24 months to come online. Lead times are therefore unlikely to improve before late 2027 at the earliest.

ABF Substrates
ABF substrate capacity is not coming online fast enough to keep up with the sharp rise in demand. The supply-demand gap is unlikely to close in the near term, so the market should stay tight. ABF substrate prices are expected to rise 10–15% QoQ starting in 3Q26 and continuing through 4Q27.

MLCC
Demand for low-end consumer-grade MLCCs is slowing, while high-end 0805 standard parts for AI applications are in short supply, extending the polarization in market demand.

author: ren_stocks
text:
I had the chance to check out J.P. Morgan's latest Memory Market Update and it only made me more bullish on 
$MU
 and 
$SNDK
.

Memory bears are running out of years to be right.

Micron now sees supply tighter in 2027 and 2028 than in 2026, with no line of sight to balance. Demand keeps outgrowing supply, and there aren't enough cleanrooms to close the gap.

Look at what customers are signing. Micron went from 16 long-term supply agreements to 26 in a single quarter, with order visibility now reaching 2031. Prepayments climbed to $32B from $22B, the contracted backlog sits at $150B, and about 75% of 2027 output is already locked in.

HBM is even tighter. 2027 supply is sold out with prices up 54% y/y, and bit demand is growing 63% against 37% for the rest of server memory.

This goes well beyond Micron. Samsung has 60 to 70% of its plant capacity under contract and SK Hynix is signing five-year terms.

You only prepay $32B years ahead when the bigger risk is ending up with no supply.

Cycles end when supply catches up, and right now nobody in this industry can tell you when that happens.

Bullish memory
